legacy_cells.B: A Bayesian Deep Learning Framework for End-To-End Prediction of Emotion From Heartbeat
legacy_cells.I: 025_2022_A Bayesian Deep Learning Framework for End-To-End Prediction of Emotion From Heartbeat.pdf
legacy_cells.AJ: Parallel streams: four stacked 1D convolutional layers with global average pooling; bidirectional LSTM; concatenation and dense valence readout
legacy_cells.FL: IBI time series → parallel CNN and bidirectional LSTM streams → concatenation → dense valence regression/classification readout; MC dropout estimates predictive uncertainty; no state transition or planner.
legacy_cells.FM: End-to-end valence classification from unimodal IBI data, with an MC-dropout Bayesian framework and adjustable confidence-based prediction acceptance/rejection.
legacy_cells.FN: The abstract reports peak classification accuracy of 90%; results state that increasing the confidence threshold increased accuracy while reducing coverage.
legacy_cells.FP: The authors identify future applications to emotional arousal, discrete emotion models, multimodal input, and multimodal output.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify limited physiological-signal emotion-prediction work and note that temporal modelling of peripheral physiological signals is rare.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence is limited to retrospective subject-wise cross-validation of valence classification on two existing datasets. The experiments do not demonstrate a persistent patient state, temporal state transitions, treatment effects, counterfactuals, planning, or clinical utility.
legacy_cells.FT: A confidence threshold with an explicit reject option can expose a coverage–accuracy trade-off; this supports uncertainty-aware classification, not treatment or state-transition simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: PDF pp. 1–2: title, abstract, introduction, related work; pp. 3–4: Bayesian framework, model architecture, data, preprocessing, training and evaluation methods; pp. 5–6: results and Table II; p. 7: discussion and conclusion; p. 8: references. The complete eight-page extracted text was reviewed. | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: The PDF directly contradicts metadata year 2022 (copyright/DOI year 2020) and gives the exact title capitalization; B and D were corrected. Table II text extraction has column-alignment ambiguity, so no table-specific metric was transcribed; the reported 90% peak accuracy is quoted from the abstract. No standalone limitations section appears; discussion and conclusion were read. Evidence QA: 2/28 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (7.1%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Schema normalization (source details retained): DU normalized to 'Patient-level split'; source detail: 10-fold leave-one-subject-out cross-validation Codex audit: 32 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 2 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis. Prior unsupported/missing fields remain Not reported; no clinical benefit inferred from offline simulation.

limitations: All8 physical pages,67references and author bios read; all pages rendered. Figures1–4 and TablesI–II visually inspected pages3–6. No appendix included.

Peak0.90 AMIGOS/0.86 DREAMER at alpha0.9 applies accepted subset with reduced coverage, not full population. Exact coverage not transcribed from approximate plot; selected samples fewer, no clinical threshold validation.
10-fold leave-one-subject-out wording ambiguous against40/25participants; exact train/test subject allocation/repetition not supplied. Subject-separation intent clear.

Existing healthy-participant datasets, not prospective mental health diagnosis or clinician escalation. No cross-dataset transfer, independent replication or human review.
